correctness.rationale: For an arbitrary n-vertex connected diameter-at-most-two graph, a k-part partition has at most k unordered block-distance codes, forcing k=n; then connected vertex degrees take at most n−1 positive values, so two singleton-part codes agree. The finite sharp-onset claim exhausts all 2^6, 2^10 and 2^15 labelled simple edge sets at orders 4,5,6, with complete BFS and every Bell-number partition, and verifies 720 positive six-vertex graphs are all isomorphic to the witness. Its two five-block bases and failure of all other block counts are checked directly from this embedded verifier. Independent check against the graph atlas agreed on the unique isomorphism class. Unrestricted theorem is not inferred from experiments.

value.rationale: The general theorem classifies an entire diameter stratum of the newly defined multiset partition parameter and subsumes several prior family-by-family impossible examples. Its sharp boundary is characterized with a complete first-order graph census, a unique asymmetric six-vertex witness and all two optimum partitions, and it exhibits failure of refinement monotonicity. The six-vertex cutoff is forced by minimality at the first attainable diameter, not arbitrarily chosen. The result is a motivated structural boundary and natural complete small extremal classification, not merely an isolated code table.
